options: A report listing every receipt method configured in the system
The central place a collector works from, consolidating aging, dunning history, and customer tools
A tool exclusively for processing lockbox exceptions
The screen used to configure GL accounts
questions.explain: The Collections Workbench gives a collector a consolidated view of a customer's aging, dunning history, and the tools to print statements or letters.

questions.q: What drives the escalation of letters under aged dunning?
options: The time since the last dunning letter was sent
How old the customer's single oldest past-due transaction is
The customer's credit limit
The receipt method assigned to the customer
questions.explain: Aged dunning escalates based on how far past due the customer's oldest open transaction is, rather than the timing of prior letters.

questions.q: What drives the escalation of letters under staged dunning?
options: How old the oldest past-due transaction is
The number of transactions the customer currently has open
How long it has been since the last dunning letter was sent
The customer's payment terms
questions.explain: Staged dunning is based on the time elapsed since the last letter, following a set cadence regardless of which transaction is oldest.

questions.q: What typically happens as a dunning program moves to higher levels?
options: The letters become friendlier and less specific
The letters escalate in tone, from a friendly reminder to a formal warning of credit hold or collections referral
The customer's balance is automatically written off
The customer is automatically merged with another account
questions.explain: Dunning levels typically escalate from a polite first reminder to progressively firmer notices, ending in a formal warning.

questions.q: At what levels can dunning be configured?
options: Only at the overall company level
Only at the individual transaction level
At the customer, account, or individual bill-to site level
Only at the General Ledger level
questions.explain: Dunning can be scoped at the customer, account, or bill-to site level, which matters for large customers with multiple divisions or locations.
